It does not cover the 2023 target year. Does not cover 2023 target year or any actual governance implementation. Biography is a sympathetic academic profile; author-editor position is not declared."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5","5B.7","5B.8"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0002","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"During the 2000-2005 DF government, López Obrador implemented the 'Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores' (Universal Food Pension for the Elderly), distributing benefits to elderly residents of Mexico City — a social program targeting a vulnerable group (elders). The municipal government declined to implement Seguro Popular, arguing DF residents already received free municipal social coverage.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"mixed","actor":"López Obrador as Head of Government of Mexico City (DF)","action":"implemented Universal Food Pension for Elderly while declining to implement Seguro Popular national health program","mechanism":"municipal social spending program; refusal to implement federal health program","outcome":"Elderly DF residents received direct food pension; DF residents did not receive Seguro Popular coverage available elsewhere in Mexico","dates":["2000-2005"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"los mexiqueños se beneficiaron de varios programas de protección social, el más destacado de los cuales fue la Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores. El Gobierno municipal se resistió a implementar el Seguro Popular, aprobado por el Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (IMSS) y basado en la aportaciones de cuotas por los beneficiarios, aduciendo que los defeños ya recibían de sus instituciones municipales la necesaria cobertura social y además gratuita.","locator":"extracted HTML block 21","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"DF government (2000-2005) predates the 2023 target year; provides governance philosophy evidence. Campaign-era program content (unit-0062) indicates these pension policies were reprised at the national level.","source_limitations":["2000-2005 DF governance predates 2023 target year. Seguro Popular refusal was a municipal policy, not a federal one."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0003","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"In March 2004, Televisa broadcast clandestine videos ('videoescándalo') showing López Obrador's close collaborators — Gustavo Ponce Meléndez (DF Finance Secretary), René Bejarano (his former chief of staff and PRD legislative coordinator), and Carlos Ímaz (Tlalpan delegation head) — gambling thousands of dollars at Las Vegas casinos and negotiating/collecting cash payments from businessman Carlos Ahumada Kurtz. All three were charged with fraud and money laundering. Rosario Robles (PRD president 2002-2003) was forced to leave the party. López Obrador's response was delayed and tepid, framing the scandal as a 'conspiracy' by ex-president Salinas, Fernández de Cevallos, and the Fox administration.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"adverse","actor":"Gustavo Ponce Meléndez, René Bejarano, Carlos Ímaz, Carlos Ahumada Kurtz, Rosario Robles, López Obrador","action":"caught receiving cash payments from businessman and gambling in Las Vegas casinos; López Obrador characterized exposure as political conspiracy","mechanism":"Televisa broadcast of clandestine videos; criminal charges for fraud and money laundering","outcome":"Three collaborators charged; Robles forced out of PRD; López Obrador framed scandal as political persecution rather than acknowledging corruption among his inner circle","dates":["March 2004"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"En marzo de 2004, en un momento que a muchos no les pareció casual, estalló el llamado videoescándalo, la emisión por la cadena Televisa de unas grabaciones de vídeo clandestinas que mostraban a prominentes políticos y funcionarios, la mayoría miembros del PRD y colaboradores estrechos de López Obrador, en situaciones altamente comprometedoras... Los tres habían sido grabados mientras se dedicaban a actividades lúdicas como jugarse a la ruleta miles de dólares en un lujoso casino de Las Vegas y a otras mucho más alarmantes, como negociar con Ahumada la compra de favores políticos o recoger de sus manos ingentes sumas de dinero.","locator":"extracted HTML block 22","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"March 2004 predates the 2023 target year but is directly relevant to evaluating whether López Obradar would enforce anti-corruption rules against his own political associates — a question applicable to his 2023 presidency.","source_limitations":["March 2004 predates 2023 by 19 years. This is the most directly relevant evidence in the source for 5B.5 conduct, but it concerns DF government associates, not federal-level conduct in 2023."],"question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0004","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"The 2018 campaign platform of the Juntos Haremos Historia coalition (MORENA, PT, PES) pledged 'austeridad republicana' — reorienting public resources from operating costs to investment without raising taxes, plus 100 billion pesos in first-year savings. The program included social programs targeting poverty and vulnerable groups, increased domestic gasoline production to reduce imports, energy and food self-sufficiency, anti-corruption pledges, and defense of Mexican migrants against Trump's border policies.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"López Obrador and Juntos Haremos Historia coalition","action":"promulgated 2018 campaign platform with austerity, social spending, energy self-sufficiency, and anti-corruption commitments","mechanism":"published Project 2018 / Project Alternative of Nation 2018-2024; campaign literature","outcome":"Platform formed the basis for the December 2018 inauguration and subsequent policy direction","dates":["2018 campaign period","December 2018 inauguration"],"quantities":["100,000 million pesos savings in first year promised"],"excerpt":"El programa electoral incidía en una serie de temas: la 'austeridad republicana', para reorientar los recursos públicos de los gastos corrientes a la inversión sin subir los impuestos; la atención de las 'causas sociales', combatiendo la pobreza y elevando el desarrollo humano de los colectivos vulnerables... el aumento de la oferta de gasolina autóctona para reducir las importaciones y rebajar precios; las autosuficiencias energética y alimentaria... y la defensa firme de los migrantes mexicanos.","locator":"extracted HTML block 5","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"The source was published November 2018 and documents only the announced platform and early transition actions, not the executed budget outcomes of 2023. There is a 4+ year gap between the announced program and the target year.","source_limitations":["Campaign platform announced in 2018 — a promise, not an executed record. No evidence of actual 2023 budget composition or execution is available from this source. The biography cannot evaluate implementation."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0005","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"López Obrador publicly pledged that anti-corruption enforcement under his presidency would include no persecution or vengeance: 'We declare emphatically that what is needed is justice, not revenge, we hate no one' and 'I am not going to put Peña Nieto in jail.' Truth Commissions would investigate FOBAPROA and PEMEX without criminal prosecution of individuals.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"mixed","actor":"López Obrador (as president-elect and candidate)","action":"pledged justice without vengeance, no persecution, and Truth Commissions rather than prosecutions for former presidents","mechanism":"campaign speeches; victory speech; IV Congress presentation November 2017","outcome":"Promise of limited accountability for prior administrations; explicit commitment against prosecutorial pursuit of ex-presidents","dates":["November 2017 (IV Congress)","16 March 2018 (INE registration)","July 2018 (victory speech)"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"'Declaramos enfáticamente que lo que se necesita es justicia, no venganza, no odiamos a nadie', subrayó el candidato... 'No voy a meter a Peña Nieto en la cárcel', aseguró también durante la campaña... las investigaciones para el esclarecimiento de los abusos incluirían el caso del FOBAPROA y a Pemex, objetos de escrutinio por sendas comisiones de la verdad aunque, eso sí, no habría 'persecución contra nadie'.","locator":"extracted HTML block 60","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"November 2017 campaign period; does not cover 2023 actual anti-corruption enforcement record. Cannot evaluate whether this pledge was kept or violated in 2023.","source_limitations":["Campaign-period pledge, not an observed governance outcome. No evidence in source of actual 2023 anti-corruption enforcement. Biography published November 2018."],"question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0006","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"In his July 2018 victory speech, López Obrador pledged: 'No mentir, no robar, no traicionar al pueblo' (not to lie, not to steal, not to betray the people); promised corruption eradication regardless of position ('incluye a compañeros de lucha, funcionarios, amigos y familiares'); and declared 'por el bien de todos, primero los pobres' (for the good of all, the poor first). The coalition won supermajorities in both federal chambers: 308/500 deputies and 69/128 senators.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"López Obrador","action":"made explicit anti-corruption and pro-poor priority pledges in victory speech; MORENA coalition secured legislative supermajority","mechanism":"victory speech at Zócalo; July 2018 election results","outcome":"Legislative supermajority enabling passage of MORENA agenda; explicit corruption eradication pledge with universal application","dates":["2 July 2018 (victory speech)","July 2018 (congressional elections)"],"quantities":["308/500 deputies","69/128 senators","53.19% of presidential vote"],"excerpt":"'Bajo ninguna circunstancia, el próximo presidente permitirá la corrupción ni la impunidad. Sobre aviso no hay engaño: sea quien sea, será castigado. Incluyo a compañeros de lucha, funcionarios, amigos y familiares'... 'Por el bien de todos, primero los pobres'... en la Cámara de Diputados, los tres partidos de Juntos Haremos Historia sumaban 308 escaños de 500 y en el Senado 69 escaños de 128.","locator":"extracted HTML block 65","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"July 2018 election and victory speech; provides stated governance priorities and mandate scope. Does not cover 2023 actual conduct or outcomes.","source_limitations":["Victory speech pledge, not an observed 2023 outcome. Biography published November 2018 does not cover 2023 execution of these pledges."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5","5B.7","5B.8"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0007","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"The 2018 campaign platform characterized López Obrador's governance philosophy as 'pragmatic social democracy' accepting free market principles, macroeconomic stability, budget discipline, peso floatation, and Bank of Mexico autonomy, combined with rejection of neoliberalism, privatization, and foreign takeover of strategic sectors, prioritizing national production and domestic consumption. He promised to create the National Guard, pursue Santa Lucía Airport (not NAIM), provide free internet nationwide, implement gender equality in labor, and run the Becas Estudiantiles 'Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro' youth employment program.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"mixed","actor":"López Obrador and MORENA coalition","action":"articulated hybrid economic philosophy combining market orthodoxy with nationalist protectionism and announced specific infrastructure and social program commitments","mechanism":"Project Alternative of Nation 2018-2024; campaign presentations","outcome":"Framework for 2018-2024 presidency combining macroeconomic discipline with state-directed development and social welfare","dates":["November 2017 (IV Congress)","2018 campaign"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Su plataforma para el período de gobierno 2018-2024 sugiere una socialdemocracia pragmática que asume las nociones ortodoxas del libre mercado, la estabilidad macroeconómica, la disciplina presupuestaria y la flotación del peso, conjugadas, eso sí, con el rechazo a las 'tendencias privatizadoras' y la 'extranjerización' de sectores estratégicos, y la prioridad para la 'producción nacional'.","locator":"extracted HTML block 6","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"Campaign-period policy framework announcement (November 2017 to 2018). Does not cover 2023 actual policy execution or outcomes. The biography was published November 2018.","source_limitations":["Announced policy framework, not observed 2023 governance outcomes. No evidence of actual macroeconomic management, regulatory enforcement, or budget execution in 2023 is available from this source."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0008","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"López Obrador lost the July 2006 presidential election to Felipe Calderón by 0.58% (243,934 votes) — 35.89% to 35.31%. He rejected the result, claimed electoral fraud, self-proclaimed himself 'president legítimo' leading an alternate government, and launched non-violent civil disobedience. The EU observer mission and international community recognized Calderón's victory. This pattern of rejecting electoral defeats was repeated in 2012.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"adverse","actor":"López Obrador; Felipe Calderón; EU election observation mission; international community","action":"rejected narrow electoral defeat; declared self as 'president legítimo'; launched civil disobedience; international community recognized opponent's victory","mechanism":"rejection of official electoral result; parallel government declaration; civil disobedience campaign","outcome":"International community recognized Calderón; credibility of electoral institutions challenged by candidate; parallel government operated","dates":["July 2006 election","August-September 2006"],"quantities":["0.58% margin (243,934 votes)","35.89% vs 35.31%"],"excerpt":"Sin embargo, la victoria del panista fue reconocida por toda la comunidad internacional... se autoproclamó 'presidente legítimo', al frente del 'Gobierno alterno' de México y en lugar del 'espurio' Calderón.","locator":"extracted HTML block 3","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"2006 and 2012 predirect 2023 by 11-17 years, but demonstrate a behavioral pattern of rejecting adverse electoral results that bears on 5B.7 (reliable information vs. slogans/denial) and potentially on governance credibility in 2023.","source_limitations":["2006 and 2012 events predate 2023 by 11-17 years. These are historical behavioral patterns, not 2023 governance evidence. The source does not cover whether this pattern persisted into the 2023 presidency."],"question_ids":["5B.7","5B.5"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0009","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"During the 2018 USMCA trade renegotiation and migration crisis, López Obrador's administration offered work visas to Central American migrants while Trump threatened to 'permanently' close the US border in November 2018, which would have caused enormous commercial damage to Mexico. López Obrador considered the USMCA beneficial for Mexico.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"mixed","actor":"López Obradar; Trump administration; US and Mexican governments","action":"negotiated USMCA; responded to migration caravans with work visa offers; faced Trump border closure threat","mechanism":"diplomatic negotiations; migration policy; trade treaty negotiation","outcome":"USMCA ratified as beneficial for Mexico; migration tensions managed through visa policy without border closure","dates":["2018 (USMCA negotiation period)","October-November 2018 (migration caravan crisis)"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Si por un lado las negociaciones con Washington y Ottawa ya han perfilado el nuevo tratado comercial trilateral que sustituirá al TLCAN, el USMCA, y que López Obrador considera beneficioso, México es en estos momentos el país de tránsito de unas caravanas de miles de migrantes irregulares centroamericanos... El 26 de noviembre, tras un intento de asalto repelido con gases lacrimógenos por la Policía estadounidense, Trump amenazó con cerrar la frontera 'permanentemente', lo que de suceder acarrearía enormes daños comerciales a México.","locator":"extracted HTML block 7","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"2018 late transition/early administration period; provides evidence on external shock management approach. Does not cover 2023 shock response directly.","source_limitations":["2018 transition period; 4+ years before 2023. No evidence of actual 2023 shock management (inflation, debt, commodity shocks) available from this source."],"question_ids":["5B.9"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0010","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"López Obradar left the PRD in September 2012 after disputes with party leadership, founded MORENA as his own political movement, refused to join the bipartisan 'Pacto por México' agreement, and consistently opposed Peña Nieto's structural reforms (energy, education, labor, telecommunications), characterizing the PRI-PAN duopoly as corrupt, weak, and incompetent.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"context","actor":"López Obradar; PRD; MORENA; Peña Nieto administration","action":"founded MORENA; refused bipartisan consensus agreement; opposed structural reforms; characterized political establishment as corrupt","mechanism":"party split; parliamentary opposition; public political statements","outcome":"MORENA established as opposition party; bipartisan governance agreements bypassed; energy and other structural reforms opposed","dates":["September 2012","2012-2018 (opposition period)"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"En septiembre de 2012, poniendo colofón a sus desavenencias con la cúpula del partido... López Obrador dio portazo a un PRD... Con MORENA, AMLO redobló su batalla contra casi todo el mundo. Así, rehusó sumarse al Pacto por México suscrito por el PRI, el PAN y el PRD; declaró su hostilidad a las grandes reformas estructurales de Peña Nieto.","locator":"extracted HTML block 4","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"2012-2018 opposition period; provides evidence of policy stance on structural reforms (energy, competition) and opposition to consensus governance. Relevant to 5B.4 and 5B.1 as behavioral context, but not 2023 executive governance.","source_limitations":["Opposition period (2012-2018) predates 2023 presidency. Demonstrates policy positions but not executive governance conduct in 2023."],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.5"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0011","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"During the 2018 campaign, López Obradar explicitly distanced himself from the Venezuelan model: 'I have nothing to do with the Government of Venezuela' and 'my Mexicanism means neither Chavismo nor Trumpism.' He rejected any association with Chávez, stating he had no personal or institutional relationship with the Venezuelan leader.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"exculpatory","actor":"López Obradar","action":"explicitly rejected association with Chávez/Venezuela and with Trumpism, defining Mexican nationalism as a third path","mechanism":"campaign statements; IV Congress presentation; public speeches","outcome":"Clear ideological differentiation from Venezuelan populist model and from Trump-style nationalism","dates":["2018 campaign period"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Su plataforma para el período de gobierno 2018-2024 sugiere una socialdemocracia pragmática... Al final, el líder opuesto convenció con su promesa de 'ser como Benito Juárez, Francisco Madero y Lázaro Cárdenas, un hombre de nación', y con su insistencia en 'no tener nada que ver con el Gobierno de Venezuela', pues su 'mexicanismo' equivalía a decir 'ni chavismo, ni trumpismo'.","locator":"extracted HTML block 6","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obrador', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"2018 campaign positioning; provides stated ideological framework but not 2023 governance record.","source_limitations":["Campaign-period ideological statement, not a 2023 governance outcome. He opposed Peña Nieto's energy reform as privatization.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"López Obradar and MORENA","action":"promised to protect state energy monopoly, build refineries, reverse privatization, and develop renewables","mechanism":"campaign platform commitments; Project Alternative of Nation 2018-2024","outcome":"State energy sovereignty pledges; opposition to private participation in energy sector","dates":["2012 campaign","2018 campaign (Project 2018)"],"quantities":["three refineries promised"],"excerpt":"Para López Obradar, era imperativo blindar la titularidad estatal de Pemex, poniendo 'toda la producción y la transformación de los hidrocarburos al servicio exclusivo de la nación'... Como medidas concretas, el decálogo perredista proponía la exploración y explotación de todas las reservas petrolíferas viables, la construcción de tres grandes refinerías para reducir las importaciones y más formación de capital humano nacional.","locator":"extracted HTML block 47","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obradar', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"Campaign-period policy pledges (2012 and 2018). These were reprised from the 2012 platform.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"López Obradar and MORENA","action":"promised specific quantitative social and economic targets for 2018-2024 sexenio","mechanism":"campaign platform; Project Alternative of Nation 2018-2024","outcome":"Specific quantitative governance targets announced for growth, employment, wages, social protection","dates":["2012 platform; reiterated in 2018 campaign"],"quantities":["6% annual growth promised","1.2 million jobs per year promised","minimum wage increases above inflation promised","pensions for all adults over 68 promised","pensions for all persons with disabilities promised"],"excerpt":"En el terreno socioeconómico, el candidato ofrecía un ramillete de compromisos: obtener una tasa de crecimiento 'incluyente' del 6% anual (el triple de promedio registrado en los 12 años de administraciones panistas)... generar 1,2 millones de empleos al año... elevar los salarios mínimos por encima de la inflación... dar cobertura pública universal en todos los niveles educativos, incluido el universitario, así como en el acceso a los servicios de salud y en las prestaciones de pensiones a todos los adultos mayores de 68 años y a todas las personas con discapacidad.","locator":"extracted HTML block 48","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obradar', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"Campaign-period promises reprised from 2012 and repeated in 2018. The coalition slogan 'Por el Bien de Todos' included the tagline 'primero los pobres.' The PAN ran advertising stating 'López Obradar is a danger to Mexico.'","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"mixed","actor":"PRD-led Coalition Por el Bien de Todos; PAN opposition","action":"promised regime change, anti-corruption framework, austerity, and pro-poor policies; opposition characterized candidate as national danger","mechanism":"coalition campaign program; opposition advertising","outcome":"AMLO lost 2006 election narrowly; framework represented continuity in progressive economic platform","dates":["2005-2006 presidential campaign"],"quantities":["presidential salary to be halved","100,000 million pesos first-year savings promised"],"excerpt":"El programa de la coalición Por el Bien de Todos... En primer lugar, había que poner fin al estado de 'privilegios', 'corrupción' y 'saqueo' patrocinado desde la Administración federal... las corruptelas tendrían que ser barridas 'como se barren las escaleras, de arriba para abajo'. A la vez, urgía combatir el fraude y la evasión fiscal, así como recortar drásticamente los gastos corrientes, siendo el primer paso la reducción a la mitad del sueldo del presidente de la República. En cuanto a las actividades del FOBAPROA, serían investigadas por una Comisión de la Verdad.","locator":"extracted HTML block 30","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obradar', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"2006 campaign period; 12 years before 2023 target year. He used these to promote accountability and transparency. This practice was reprised as a presidential tool after December 2018.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"López Obradar as DF Head of Government","action":"held daily 6:00 AM press conferences for accountability and transparency","mechanism":"daily morning press conferences (las mañaneras)","outcome":"Set national political agenda; promoted transparency; became signature governance communication tool","dates":["2000-2005 (DF government)","reprised from December 2018 onward"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Sus conferencias de prensa a la temprana, por no decir intempestiva, hora de las seis de la mañana, conocidas popularmente como las mañaneras, generaban invariablemente una inusitada expectación periodística y marcaron la agenda política del país.","locator":"extracted HTML block 20","attribution":"CIDOB, 'Andrés Manuel López Obradar', edited by Roberto Ortiz de Zárate Arce, published 29/11/2018","period_fit":"2000-2005 DF governance period; demonstrates transparency communication practice.
